focal_entities.audience: the user at the goal sign-off, approving what the finished work will do and why, and rn's orchestrator in any later conversation, carrying the work on without asking them again

goal_orientation.purpose: approving the goal and the acceptance criteria, then carrying each later work to them

constraints.decision: Purpose: The user cannot quickly find the file they want in their Downloads folder; the tool sorts its files by kind so they are easy to find.

How files are sorted: The tool creates a folder for each kind (such as Images, Documents) inside the Downloads folder and moves files into it. Only files directly in the Downloads folder are handled. It only moves files: it never deletes, renames or overwrites anything.
Kinds: A file's kind is told by its extension, sorted into broad kinds: Images, Documents, Videos, Audio, Archives, Installers, Code, and Others for files that fit none.

Same name in the kind's folder: When the kind's folder already holds a file of the same name, the file is not moved: it stays directly in Downloads, and the tool shows that it was left because a file of the same name is there.
Preview before moving: Run with no option, the tool only previews: it shows which file would move to which folder and moves nothing. It moves files only when an option tells it to.
Systems it runs on: The tool runs on macOS and Linux; Windows is not needed.
Folder it works on: By default the tool works on ~/Downloads; an argument can name another folder instead.

Hidden and unfinished files: Hidden files (names starting with a dot, such as .DS_Store) and files a browser is still downloading (such as .crdownload, .part, .download) are never moved, so the system and downloads in progress are not broken.

What shows it done: On a test folder holding files of each kind, a file whose name is already in its kind's folder, hidden files, unfinished downloads and a subfolder, on macOS and on Linux each: a preview moves nothing, and the move option moves files as decided, with no file deleted, renamed or overwritten. The README says how to install the tool and how to use it. Tests check what was decided.
